components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 每年春节,他都会回老家看望父母。
example.pinyin: Měinián Chūnjié, tā dōu huì huí lǎojiā kànwàng fùmǔ.
example.english: Every Spring Festival, he goes back to his hometown to visit his parents.
example.fact: Chunyun, the Chinese New Year travel rush, is considered the largest annual human migration on Earth, with an estimated three billion trips made across China in a single travel season. Most travelers are returning to their home regions to be with family.

examples.hanzi: 我老家在一个很小的山村。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎojiā zài yí gè hěn xiǎo de shāncūn.
examples.english: My hometown is in a very small mountain village.

examples.hanzi: 你的老家是哪儿的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de lǎojiā shì nǎr de?
examples.english: Where is your hometown?

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.hanzi: 在物理学中,爱因斯坦提出了相对论。
example.pinyin: Zài wùlǐxué zhōng, Àiyīnsītǎn tíchū le xiāngduìlùn.
example.english: In physics, Einstein proposed the theory of relativity.
example.fact: Einstein's theory of general relativity, published in 1915, predicts that massive objects bend spacetime. That prediction was confirmed in 1919 when astronomers observed starlight bending around the sun during a total solar eclipse.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店相对便宜，但是离市中心比较远。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn xiāngduì piányi, dànshì lí shì zhōngxīn bǐjiào yuǎn.
examples.english: This hotel is relatively cheap, but it is rather far from downtown.

examples.hanzi: 好和坏都是相对的。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo hé huài dōu shì xiāngduì de.
examples.english: Good and bad are both relative.

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — plain unmixed thread, hence pure; also in 红 red, 级 level.
屯 (tún) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 钝 dùn and 顿 dùn.

example.hanzi: 孩子的想法往往很单纯。
example.pinyin: Háizi de xiǎngfǎ wǎngwǎng hěn dānchún.
example.english: Children's thoughts are often very simple and pure.
example.fact: Diamond and graphite are both made of pure carbon in its simplest elemental form. Yet the different arrangement of their atoms gives one unmatched hardness and the other enough softness to write with.

examples.hanzi: 我只是单纯想帮你，没有别的意思。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐshì dānchún xiǎng bāng nǐ, méiyǒu bié de yìsi.
examples.english: I simply want to help you; I have no other intention.

examples.hanzi: 她是个单纯的女孩，容易相信别人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè dānchún de nǚhái, róngyì xiāngxìn biérén.
examples.english: She is a naive girl who easily trusts others.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — a tube was first a length of bamboo; marks bamboo things, as in 笔 pen, 筷 chopsticks.
同 (tóng) — close sound: 筒 tǒng. 同 also sounds out 铜 tóng and 桶 tǒng.

example.hanzi: 他把画卷起来放进纸筒里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ huà juǎn qǐlái fàng jìn zhǐtǒng lǐ.
example.english: He rolled up the painting and put it in a paper tube.
example.fact: 筒 appears in 笔筒 (pen holder), 垃圾筒 (trash can), 手电筒 (flashlight). It originally meant a piece of bamboo tube.

examples.hanzi: 你把雨伞放进伞筒里吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bǎ yǔsǎn fàng jìn sǎntǒng lǐ ba.
examples.english: Put your umbrella in the umbrella stand.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一支笔筒里的笔。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhī bǐtǒng lǐ de bǐ.
examples.english: Please give me a pen from the pen holder.

components.note: 门 (gate) — a wooden bar 木 across a gate: 闲 was a fence, and now means idle, as in 空闲 free time.

example.hanzi: 周末我很闲。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ hěn xián.
example.english: I'm free this weekend.
example.fact: 闲 means being idle or having nothing to do: 闲聊 (chat), 悠闲 (leisurely), 闲逛 (stroll). 有空 is a more neutral way to say you're free.

examples.hanzi: 你今天有空闲时间吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān yǒu kòngxián shíjiān ma?
examples.english: Do you have any free time today?

examples.hanzi: 他退休后，每天都很清闲。
examples.pinyin: Tā tuìxiū hòu, měitiān dōu hěn qīngxián.
examples.english: After retiring, he is at leisure every day.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand 爫 reaching down to a tree 木 to pick its fruit or leaves — to gather, as in 采访.

example.hanzi: 我们去山上采蘑菇。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù shān shang cǎi mógu.
example.english: We're going up the mountain to pick mushrooms.
example.fact: 采 gives 采访 (interview), 采用 (adopt), 采购 (purchase). Don't confuse it with 彩 (colour) or 踩 (to step on).

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢在森林里采蘑菇。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài sēnlín lǐ cǎi mógu.
examples.english: She likes picking mushrooms in the forest.

examples.hanzi: 记者今天去采访了一位老教授。
examples.pinyin: Jìzhě jīntiān qù cǎifǎng le yí wèi lǎo jiàoshòu.
examples.english: The reporter went to interview an old professor today.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 他是个很老实的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì gè hěn lǎoshi de rén.
example.english: He is a very honest person.
example.fact: 实 gives 老实 (honest), 事实 (fact), 实现 (achieve), 现实 (reality), 实习 (internship) and 其实 (actually). It can also mean 'fruit' in 果实.

examples.hanzi: 你说的话是真实的吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de huà shì zhēnshí de ma?
examples.english: Are the things you said true?

examples.hanzi: 我们要把计划变成现实。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎ jìhuà biànchéng xiànshí.
examples.english: We want to turn the plan into reality.

components.note: 京 (jīng) — capital, drawn as a tall building on a mound; as a part it sounds out 景 jǐng, 惊 jīng, 鲸 jīng and 凉 liáng.

example.hanzi: 他去年搬到了北京。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián bān dào le Běijīng.
example.english: He moved to Beijing last year.
example.fact: 京 means 'capital': 北京 (northern capital), 南京 (southern capital), 东京 (Tokyo, 'eastern capital') and 京剧 (Peking opera).

examples.hanzi: 北京的冬天很冷。
examples.pinyin: Běijīng de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
examples.english: Winter in Beijing is very cold.

examples.hanzi: 我明年想去南京看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián xiǎng qù Nánjīng kànkan.
examples.english: Next year I want to go to Nanjing.

components.note: 曲 (bent) — the shape pictures something bent; qū means crooked and qǔ means a song, as in 歌曲.
木 (wood) — a wooden stick; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
昆 (kūn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 混 hùn.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.hanzi: 曲棍球是一项需要团队合作的运动。
example.pinyin: Qūgùnqiú shì yī xiàng xūyào tuánduì hézuò de yùndòng.
example.english: Field hockey is a sport that requires teamwork.
example.fact: Field hockey is believed to have origins stretching back over 4,000 years, with stick-and-ball games depicted in ancient Egyptian tomb art at Beni Hasan. That makes it one of the oldest team sports still played today.

examples.hanzi: 冬天，我们在冰上打曲棍球。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān, wǒmen zài bīng shàng dǎ qūgùnqiú.
examples.english: In winter we play hockey on the ice.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥是学校曲棍球队的队员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge shì xuéxiào qūgùnqiú duì de duìyuán.
examples.english: My older brother is on the school hockey team.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.hanzi: 书架上好些书都还没有看完。
example.pinyin: Shūjià shàng hǎoxiē shū dōu hái méiyǒu kàn wán.
example.english: There are quite a lot of books on the shelf that haven't been finished yet.
example.fact: The Library of Congress in Washington, D.C. holds more than 170 million items across its collections, including books, manuscripts, maps, and recordings. That makes it the largest library in the world by shelf space.

examples.hanzi: 好些人都说这家店的面很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Hǎoxiē rén dōu shuō zhè jiā diàn de miàn hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: Quite a few people say the noodles at this shop are delicious.

examples.hanzi: 他已经好些年没回过家了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng hǎoxiē nián méi huí guo jiā le.
examples.english: He hasn't been home for quite a few years.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.

example.hanzi: 记者必须核实消息来源是否可信。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě bìxū héshí xiāoxī láiyuán shìfǒu kěxìn.
example.english: Journalists must verify whether their sources are trustworthy.
example.fact: Fact-checking as an organized newsroom practice dates back to the 1920s at magazines like Time, where dedicated checkers verified every factual claim in an article before publication. The practice was created specifically to protect the outlet's credibility.

examples.hanzi: 他这个人说话很可信。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhège rén shuōhuà hěn kěxìn.
examples.english: What he says is quite trustworthy.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息听起来不太可信。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi tīng qǐlái bú tài kěxìn.
examples.english: This news doesn't sound very credible.

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.
生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的总资产超过十亿美元。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de zǒng zīchǎn chāoguò shí yì měiyuán.
example.english: This company's total assets exceed one billion US dollars.
example.fact: Studies by valuation firm Ocean Tomo have found that intangible assets, such as patents, brand value, and data, now make up the large majority of the total market value of S&P 500 companies. That share has grown steadily since the mid-20th century, when physical assets dominated corporate balance sheets.

examples.hanzi: 他把全部资产都捐给了慈善机构。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ quánbù zīchǎn dōu juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
examples.english: He donated all of his assets to charity.

examples.hanzi: 房子是他们家最重要的资产。
examples.pinyin: Fángzi shì tāmen jiā zuì zhòngyào de zīchǎn.
examples.english: The house is their family's most important asset.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — a metal hammer; also in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
垂 (chuí) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 捶 chuí and 睡 shuì.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他用锤子把钉子敲进木板里。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng chuízi bǎ dìngzi qiāo jìn mùbǎn lǐ.
example.english: He used a hammer to knock the nail into the board.
example.fact: Stone hammerstones found at the Lomekwi site in Kenya date back roughly 3.3 million years, predating the genus Homo. That suggests an even earlier hominin species crafted them, making hammers among the oldest tools known.

examples.hanzi: 请把锤子递给我。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chuízi dì gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please hand me the hammer.

examples.hanzi: 工具箱里有锤子和螺丝刀。
examples.pinyin: Gōngjùxiāng lǐ yǒu chuízi hé luósīdāo.
examples.english: There are a hammer and a screwdriver in the toolbox.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.
十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".

example.hanzi: 乔治·布什曾任美国第41任总统。
example.pinyin: Qiáozhì Bùshí céng rèn Měiguó dì sìshíyī rèn zǒngtǒng.
example.english: George Bush once served as the 41st President of the United States.
example.fact: George H. W. Bush, the 41st U.S. president, previously served as director of the CIA and as a naval aviator during World War II. He survived after being shot down over the Pacific in 1944.

examples.hanzi: 布什先生是那家公司的董事长。
examples.pinyin: Bùshí xiānsheng shì nà jiā gōngsī de dǒngshìzhǎng.
examples.english: Mr. Bush is the chairman of that company.

examples.hanzi: 新闻里正在报道布什的演讲。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén lǐ zhèngzài bàodào Bùshí de yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: The news is reporting on Bush's speech.

components.note: 录 (lù) gives sound to 绿 lǜ, 禄 lù and 碌 lù; as a word it means to record.
耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.hanzi: 她被那所大学录取了,全家都很高兴。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi nà suǒ dàxué lùqǔ le, quánjiā dōu hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: She was admitted to that university, and the whole family was delighted.
example.fact: Harvard University's undergraduate admission rate has fallen below 4% in recent years. That makes it one of the most selective universities in the world despite receiving tens of thousands of applications annually.

examples.hanzi: 他终于收到了公司的录取通知。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú shōudào le gōngsī de lùqǔ tōngzhī.
examples.english: He finally received the company's offer.

examples.hanzi: 这个专业今年只录取五十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhuānyè jīnnián zhǐ lùqǔ wǔshí gè xuésheng.
examples.english: This major admits only fifty students this year.

components.note: 东 (east) — simplified from 東; a common memory aid is the sun 日 caught in a tree 木 at sunrise.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 美国东部沿海地区人口非常密集。
example.pinyin: Měiguó dōngbù yánhǎi dìqū rénkǒu fēicháng mìjí.
example.english: The eastern coastal region of the United States is very densely populated.
example.fact: The eastern seaboard of the United States, stretching from Maine to Florida, is home to roughly a third of the country's population. That share of people lives on a relatively small fraction of the nation's total land area.

examples.hanzi: 这条河的东部有一片大森林。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé de dōngbù yǒu yí piàn dà sēnlín.
examples.english: East of this river there is a large forest.

examples.hanzi: 东部的城市比西部发展得更快。
examples.pinyin: Dōngbù de chéngshì bǐ xībù fāzhǎn de gèng kuài.
examples.english: The cities in the east have developed faster than those in the west.

meanings: (fig.) to make an identical copy of (a website etc)

components.note: 兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — hills, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sunny side; 隆 is high and grand.

example.hanzi: 1996年,科学家成功克隆出了一只名叫多莉的羊。
example.pinyin: 1996 nián, kēxuéjiā chénggōng kèlóng chū le yī zhī míng jiào Duōlì de yáng.
example.english: In 1996, scientists successfully cloned a sheep named Dolly.
example.fact: Dolly the sheep, born in 1996 at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, was the first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell. The breakthrough reshaped scientific and ethical debates about cloning technology.

examples.hanzi: 科学家想克隆一些濒危动物。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā xiǎng kèlóng yìxiē bīnwēi dòngwù.
examples.english: Scientists want to clone some endangered animals.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲的是克隆人的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì kèlóngrén de gùshi.
examples.english: This movie is about the story of clones.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 他大学毕业后就去国外工作了。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu jiù qù guówài gōngzuò le.
example.english: After graduating from university, he went abroad to work.
example.fact: According to UNESCO estimates, more than six million students were enrolled in higher education outside their home country in recent years. The United States, United Kingdom, and Australia rank among the most common destinations.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥现在在国外读书。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge xiànzài zài guówài dúshū.
examples.english: My older brother is studying abroad now.

examples.hanzi: 这是一部从国外进口的车。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí bù cóng guówài jìnkǒu de chē.
examples.english: This is a car imported from abroad.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 警察要求他交出驾驶证。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú tā jiāochū jiàshǐzhèng.
example.english: The police asked him to hand over his driver's license.
example.fact: At the end of World War II, Japan formally surrendered aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945. Representatives handed over signed documents of unconditional surrender to Allied commanders.

examples.hanzi: 请把手机交出来，考试时不能用。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shǒujī jiāo chūlái, kǎoshì shí bù néng yòng.
examples.english: Please hand in your phone; it can't be used during the exam.

examples.hanzi: 他不肯交出那把钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù kěn jiāochū nà bǎ yàoshi.
examples.english: He refused to hand over that key.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
酉 (wine jar) — 酉 is a fermenting jar, as in 酒, 酸, 醋; 酪 is a fermented dairy product.
各 (gè) — near sound — 酪 is lào; 各 also sounds out 络 luò and 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 这种干酪需要在地窖中陈放至少六个月。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng gānlào xūyào zài dìjiào zhōng chénfàng zhìshǎo liù gè yuè.
example.english: This cheese needs to age in a cellar for at least six months.
example.fact: Some wheels of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese are aged for over three years and can weigh close to 40 kilograms. Italian producers have even used them as loan collateral at specialized cheese banks that store and insure the aging wheels.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢把干酪放在面包上吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan bǎ gānlào fàng zài miànbāo shàng chī.
examples.english: I like eating cheese on bread.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的干酪种类特别多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de gānlào zhǒnglèi tèbié duō.
examples.english: This shop has an especially wide variety of cheeses.

components.note: 正 (zhèng) is a close sound clue for zhěng; 正 also means correct, fitting for putting things in order.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: setting things right by force.
彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.

example.hanzi: 越来越多的人选择整形手术来改善外貌。
example.pinyin: Yuè lái yuè duō de rén xuǎnzé zhěngxíng shǒushù lái gǎishàn wàimào.
example.english: More and more people are choosing plastic surgery to improve their appearance.
example.fact: Reconstructive surgery techniques for the nose date back over 2,600 years to the ancient Indian physician Sushruta. His text, the Sushruta Samhita, described skin-flap grafting methods still recognizable in modern rhinoplasty.

examples.hanzi: 她去年做了整形手术，变化很大。
examples.pinyin: Tā qùnián zuò le zhěngxíng shǒushù, biànhuà hěn dà.
examples.english: She had cosmetic surgery last year and has changed a lot.

examples.hanzi: 这家整形医院在本市很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā zhěngxíng yīyuàn zài běn shì hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This plastic surgery hospital is well known in the city.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; sand grains are tiny bits washed by water.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 沙 is shā; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 纱 shā.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上用沙子堆城堡。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng yòng shāzi duī chéngbǎo.
example.english: The children built castles out of sand on the beach.
example.fact: Construction-grade sand is in global short supply despite deserts being full of it, because desert sand grains are too round and smooth from wind erosion to bind well in concrete. Builders instead rely on angular sand mined from riverbeds and quarries.

examples.hanzi: 一粒沙子掉进了我的眼睛里。
examples.pinyin: Yí lì shāzi diào jìn le wǒ de yǎnjing lǐ.
examples.english: A grain of sand got into my eye.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋里进了很多沙子。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié lǐ jìn le hěn duō shāzi.
examples.english: There is a lot of sand in these shoes.

components.note: 卜 (divination) — cracks read on heated bones; 口 below is asking. 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.

example.hanzi: 军队迅速占领了这座城市。
example.pinyin: Jūnduì xùnsù zhànlǐng le zhè zuò chéngshì.
example.english: The army quickly occupied the city.
example.fact: Following World War II, Allied forces occupied Japan from 1945 to 1952 under General Douglas MacArthur. During that period, a new constitution renouncing war was drafted and adopted.

examples.hanzi: 这块地被一家公司占领了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dì bèi yì jiā gōngsī zhànlǐng le.
examples.english: This piece of land was taken over by a company.

examples.hanzi: 这家品牌很快占领了整个市场。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā pǐnpái hěn kuài zhànlǐng le zhěnggè shìchǎng.
examples.english: This brand quickly took over the whole market.

components.note: 亻 (person) — one who relies on arms; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
丈 (zhàng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 杖 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 他们打了一场大仗。
example.pinyin: Tāmen dǎ le yì chǎng dà zhàng.
example.english: They fought a major battle.
example.fact: 仗 means a battle: 打仗 (to fight a war), 胜仗 (a victory). It also means to rely on, as in 仗义 (loyal to friends) and 仗势欺人 (to bully using one's power).

examples.hanzi: 两个国家打了好几年仗。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng ge guójiā dǎ le hǎojǐ nián zhàng.
examples.english: The two countries fought a war for several years.

examples.hanzi: 他倚仗父亲的关系找到了工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐzhàng fùqin de guānxi zhǎodào le gōngzuò.
examples.english: He relied on his father's connections to find a job.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks garments, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 袜 is a sock.
末 (mò) is a loose hint for wà.

example.hanzi: 我的袜子破了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de wàzi pò le.
example.english: My sock has a hole.
example.fact: The measure word for socks is 双: 一双袜子. 丝袜 means silk stockings. 袜 usually appears as 袜子.

examples.hanzi: 冬天我穿厚厚的袜子。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān wǒ chuān hòuhòu de wàzi.
examples.english: In winter I wear thick socks.

examples.hanzi: 这双丝袜很容易破。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng sīwà hěn róngyì pò.
examples.english: These stockings tear easily.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱, 铁; 钩 is a hook made of metal.
勾 (gōu) — same sound: 钩 gōu. 勾 also sounds out 沟 gōu and 构 gòu.

example.hanzi: 他把外套挂在钩子上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ wàitào guà zài gōuzi shang.
example.english: He hung his coat on the hook.
example.fact: 钩 is a hook: 鱼钩 (fish hook), 钩针 (crochet needle). 打钩 means to tick a box with ✓.

examples.hanzi: 鱼被钩子钩住了。
examples.pinyin: Yú bèi gōuzi gōu zhù le.
examples.english: The fish was caught on the hook.

examples.hanzi: 他在答案旁边画了一个钩。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dá'àn pángbiān huà le yí ge gōu.
examples.english: He drew a check mark next to the answer.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and pouring, as in 河, 海, 清: 注 is to pour in.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; 主 also in 住 zhù, 柱 zhù and 驻 zhù.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 全世界的目光都注视着这场比赛。
example.pinyin: Quán shìjiè de mùguāng dōu zhùshì zhe zhè chǎng bǐsài.
example.english: The eyes of the whole world are watching this match closely.
example.fact: The peregrine falcon, whose eyesight is estimated to be up to eight times sharper than a human's, can spot prey on the ground from over a kilometer high. It then dives at speeds exceeding 300 kilometers per hour to make the catch.

examples.hanzi: 他一直注视着窗外的雨。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí zhùshì zhe chuāngwài de yǔ.
examples.english: He kept gazing at the rain outside the window.

examples.hanzi: 大家注视着舞台，等待演出开始。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā zhùshì zhe wǔtái, děngdài yǎnchū kāishǐ.
examples.english: Everyone watched the stage, waiting for the show to begin.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.hanzi: 所有的用户密码都经过加密存储。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de yònghù mìmǎ dōu jīngguò jiāmì cúnchú.
example.english: All user passwords are stored after being encrypted.
example.fact: During World War II, the German military's Enigma machine encrypted messages using rotating wheels that created billions of possible settings. Codebreakers at Bletchley Park, including Alan Turing, developed methods to crack it.

examples.hanzi: 请给这个文件加密，别让别人看到。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi zhège wénjiàn jiāmì, bié ràng biérén kàndào.
examples.english: Please encrypt this file so others can't see it.

examples.hanzi: 银行的数据都要加密保存。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng de shùjù dōu yào jiāmì bǎocún.
examples.english: All the bank's data has to be stored encrypted.

components.note: 大 (big/man) — the top part, as in 夫. Dictionary story: a big man wrapped in a long cloth, hence 'cover, set'; used in 外套 coat and 手套 glove.
镸 (long) — the bottom part, a long-hair variant of 長. Memory aid: a long cloth over a big person is a coat or cover.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的套房带有独立的客厅。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de tàofáng dài yǒu dúlì de kètīng.
example.english: This hotel's suite comes with a separate living room.
example.fact: The Royal Suite at Raffles Hotel in Singapore, opened in 1887, has hosted guests including Rudyard Kipling and Elizabeth Taylor. The hotel is also credited as the birthplace of the Singapore Sling cocktail in 1915.

examples.hanzi: 我们订了一间海景套房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dìng le yì jiān hǎijǐng tàofáng.
examples.english: We booked a sea-view suite.

examples.hanzi: 这间套房有两个卧室。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān tàofáng yǒu liǎng gè wòshì.
examples.english: This suite has two bedrooms.

components.note: 风 (wind) — storms and air, as in 飘 float; 飓 is a hurricane.
具 (jù) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 俱 jù and 惧 jù.
風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.

example.hanzi: 飓风即将登陆,居民被要求撤离。
example.pinyin: Jùfēng jíjiāng dēnglù, jūmín bèi yāoqiú chèlí.
example.english: The hurricane is about to make landfall, and residents have been ordered to evacuate.
example.fact: Hurricane Patricia in 2015 reached sustained winds of about 345 km/h (215 mph) in the eastern Pacific, making it one of the most intense tropical cyclones ever recorded at sea. It weakened significantly before making landfall.

examples.hanzi: 飓风过后，很多树都倒了。
examples.pinyin: Jùfēng guòhòu, hěn duō shù dōu dǎo le.
examples.english: After the hurricane, many trees had fallen.

examples.hanzi: 天气预报说飓风明天会来。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yùbào shuō jùfēng míngtiān huì lái.
examples.english: The weather forecast says the hurricane will arrive tomorrow.

components.note: 刂 (knife, 立刀旁) — cutting and peeling, as in 别, 刻, 剪.
录 (lù) is only a loose clue; it also sounds out 绿 lǜ and 碌 lù.
寸 (hand, also "inch") — a grasping hand seizing something; also in 对, 守, 寺.

example.hanzi: 独裁政府剥夺了公民的言论自由。
example.pinyin: dúcái zhèngfǔ bōduóle gōngmín de yánlùn zìyóu.
example.english: The dictatorial government deprived citizens of their freedom of speech.
example.fact: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations in 1948, explicitly protects freedom of expression in Article 19. Yet press-freedom watchdogs have found that in the decades since, more governments have restricted that freedom than expanded it, often through censorship, licensing controls, or outright bans on independent media.

examples.hanzi: 法院剥夺了他的驾驶资格。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn bōduó le tā de jiàshǐ zīgé.
examples.english: The court stripped him of his driving qualification.

examples.hanzi: 任何人都不能剥夺孩子受教育的权利。
examples.pinyin: Rènhé rén dōu bù néng bōduó háizi shòu jiàoyù de quánlì.
examples.english: No one can deprive a child of the right to an education.

meanings: (fig.) to spend money in large amounts

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.

example.hanzi: 他摔倒后手臂出血了。
example.pinyin: tā shuāidǎo hòu shǒubì chūxuèle.
example.english: He bled from his arm after he fell.
example.fact: The human body holds roughly five liters of blood, and a healthy adult can safely donate about half a liter at a time. The lost plasma volume is typically replaced within about 48 hours, though the red blood cells themselves take several weeks to fully regenerate.

examples.hanzi: 他的鼻子突然出血了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bízi tūrán chūxuè le.
examples.english: His nose suddenly started bleeding.

examples.hanzi: 伤口还在出血，要赶快包扎。
examples.pinyin: Shāngkǒu hái zài chūxuè, yào gǎnkuài bāozā.
examples.english: The wound is still bleeding and needs bandaging quickly.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 他的导师建议他申请那份奖学金。
example.pinyin: tā de dǎoshī jiànyì tā shēnqǐng nà fèn jiǎngxuéjīn.
example.english: His advisor suggested that he apply for that scholarship.
example.fact: The English word 'mentor' comes from Mentor, a character in Homer's Odyssey whom Odysseus entrusted to guide his son Telemachus. The term entered English usage in the 18th century and now describes any experienced advisor who guides someone less experienced.

examples.hanzi: 我的导师是一位很和蔼的教授。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de dǎoshī shì yí wèi hěn hé'ǎi de jiàoshòu.
examples.english: My advisor is a very kind professor.

examples.hanzi: 感谢导师对我论文的指导。
examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè dǎoshī duì wǒ lùnwén de zhǐdǎo.
examples.english: Thanks to my advisor for guiding my thesis.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杰 is simplified from 傑; a tall tree makes a handy picture for an outstanding person standing tall.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 这部电影被誉为导演的杰作。
example.pinyin: zhè bù diànyǐng bèi yùwéi dǎoyǎn de jiézuò.
example.english: This film is regarded as the director's masterpiece.
example.fact: Leonardo da Vinci is believed to have worked on the Mona Lisa intermittently for about 16 years and reportedly kept it with him until his death in 1519. It now hangs in the Louvre behind bulletproof glass and is viewed by millions of visitors every year.

examples.hanzi: 这幅画是那位画家的杰作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà shì nà wèi huàjiā de jiézuò.
examples.english: This painting is that painter's masterpiece.

examples.hanzi: 这座桥是现代建筑的杰作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo shì xiàndài jiànzhù de jiézuò.
examples.english: This bridge is a masterpiece of modern architecture.

meanings: sign (that sth is about to happen)

components.note: 彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking and journeys, as in 行 go, 往 toward, 得; 征 is a march or campaign.
正 (zhèng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 证 zhèng, 政 zhèng and 整 zhěng.
兆 — the cracks on a heated oracle bone, read as omens. It also sounds out 桃 táo, 挑 tiāo, 跳 tiào and 逃 táo.

example.hanzi: 头痛有时是感冒的征兆。
example.pinyin: tóutòng yǒushí shì gǎnmào de zhēngzhào.
example.english: A headache is sometimes a sign of catching a cold.
example.fact: Seismologists have observed small tremors, shifts in groundwater levels, and unusual animal behavior before some major earthquakes, but no such signal has proven reliable enough to predict exactly when or where a quake will strike, which is why earthquake prediction remains largely impossible today.

examples.hanzi: 天空乌云密布，这是暴雨的征兆。
examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng wūyún mìbù, zhè shì bàoyǔ de zhēngzhào.
examples.english: The sky is full of dark clouds, a sign of heavy rain.

examples.hanzi: 他发现这种征兆之后，立刻去了医院。
examples.pinyin: Tā fāxiàn zhè zhǒng zhēngzhào zhīhòu, lìkè qù le yīyuàn.
examples.english: After noticing this warning sign, he went to the hospital right away.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.
羽 (feather) — 翁 first meant the neck feathers of a bird; the old-man sense is later.
公 (gōng) is only a loose sound clue for wēng.

example.hanzi: 他年轻时就成了百万富翁。
example.pinyin: tā niánqīng shí jiù chéngle bǎiwàn fùwēng.
example.english: He became a millionaire while he was still young.
example.fact: John D. Rockefeller, often cited as history's first documented billionaire, built his fortune through the Standard Oil Company in the late 19th century. Adjusted for inflation, his peak net worth is estimated to have exceeded $300 billion in today's dollars.

examples.hanzi: 这位富翁把一半财产捐给了学校。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi fùwēng bǎ yíbàn cáichǎn juān gěi le xuéxiào.
examples.english: This rich man donated half of his fortune to schools.

examples.hanzi: 他想成为富翁，所以每天拼命工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi fùwēng, suǒyǐ měi tiān pīnmìng gōngzuò.
examples.english: He wants to become a rich man, so he works hard every day.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
亻 (person) — a person's precedent or example; also in 他 he, 做 do.
列 (liè) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.

example.hanzi: 这家医院上个月收治了三十个新冠病例。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā yīyuàn shàng gè yuè shōuzhìle sānshí gè xīnguān bìnglì.
example.english: This hospital admitted thirty COVID-19 cases last month.
example.fact: John Snow's 1854 map plotting cholera cases in London around a single water pump is considered a founding moment of modern epidemiology. His analysis identified the pump as the outbreak's source well before germ theory was widely accepted by the medical establishment.

examples.hanzi: 医生说这个病例很少见。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō zhège bìnglì hěn shǎojiàn.
examples.english: The doctor said this case is very rare.

examples.hanzi: 医院整理了去年所有的病例。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn zhěnglǐ le qùnián suǒyǒu de bìnglì.
examples.english: The hospital organized all of last year's case records.

components.note: 钅 (metal, from 金) — marks metals, as in 钱, 铁, 银; 销 first meant melting metal, then to sell off.
肖 (xiāo) gives the sound exactly: 销 xiāo, also in 消 xiāo and 宵 xiāo.
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand striking with a tool, as in 殴, 段; 毁 is to wreck.

example.hanzi: 警方销毁了缴获的毒品。
example.pinyin: jǐngfāng xiāohuǐle jiǎohuò de dúpǐn.
example.english: The police destroyed the confiscated drugs.
example.fact: Central banks routinely shred and destroy old, damaged banknotes withdrawn from circulation. The U.S. Federal Reserve destroys millions of dollars in worn-out bills every day, replacing them with newly printed currency of equal value.

examples.hanzi: 请把不要的文件销毁。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ bú yào de wénjiàn xiāohuǐ.
examples.english: Please destroy the documents you don't need.

examples.hanzi: 他把所有的证据都销毁了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu de zhèngjù dōu xiāohuǐ le.
examples.english: He destroyed all of the evidence.

components.note: 饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and hunger, as in 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饱 full.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 机 jī and 肌 jī.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and hunger, as in 饭 meal, 饱 full.
我 (wǒ) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 俄 é, 蛾 é and 鹅 é.

example.hanzi: 战争导致了大规模的饥饿。
example.pinyin: zhànzhēng dǎozhìle dà guīmó de jī'è.
example.english: The war led to widespread famine.
example.fact: The Irish Potato Famine of the 1840s, triggered by a potato blight fungus, is estimated to have caused around one million deaths and drove more than a million people to emigrate, permanently reshaping Ireland's population and its diaspora across North America.

examples.hanzi: 我饿了一天，现在饥饿难忍。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ è le yì tiān, xiànzài jī'è nán rěn.
examples.english: I haven't eaten all day and the hunger is now unbearable.

examples.hanzi: 很多国家仍然面临饥饿问题。
examples.pinyin: Hěn duō guójiā réngrán miànlín jī'è wèntí.
examples.english: Many countries still face the problem of hunger.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — sweet taste, as in 甜: 甚 first meant great enjoyment, then "very, extremely".

example.hanzi: 他甚至忘了自己的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā shènzhì wàng le zìjǐ de míngzi.
example.english: He even forgot his own name.
example.fact: 甚 is literary for 'very': 甚好, 不甚了解. In everyday text it is mostly seen in 甚至 (even), a very common linking word.

examples.hanzi: 他甚至连饭都忘了吃。
examples.pinyin: Tā shènzhì lián fàn dōu wàng le chī.
examples.english: He even forgot to eat.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我了解得不甚清楚。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ liǎojiě de bú shèn qīngchu.
examples.english: I do not understand this matter very clearly.

components.note: 要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.hanzi: 别担心,这不要紧。
example.pinyin: bié dānxīn, zhè bù yàojǐn.
example.english: Don't worry, it's not important.
example.fact: Survival rates for cardiac arrest drop by roughly 10 percent for every minute that passes without CPR or defibrillation, which is why paramedics refer to the first several minutes after a person collapses as the critical window for intervention.

examples.hanzi: 这件事很要紧，你一定要记住。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yàojǐn, nǐ yídìng yào jìzhù.
examples.english: This matter is important, so you must remember it.

examples.hanzi: 今天的会议没什么要紧的事。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de huìyì méi shénme yàojǐn de shì.
examples.english: There's nothing pressing about today's meeting.

meanings: variant of 陽臺|阳台[yang2 tai2]

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阴, 院, 队; 阳 is the sunny side of a hill, with 日 sun.
日 (sun) — 日 is the sun, as in 明, 晴, 时.
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 我喜欢在阳台上种花。
example.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan zài yángtái shàng zhòng huā.
example.english: I like growing flowers on the balcony.
example.fact: The English word 'balcony' entered the language from Italian balcone, ultimately traced to a Germanic word for a beam or piece of scaffolding. Balconies became a defining feature of Italian Renaissance architecture before spreading across the rest of Europe.

examples.hanzi: 我家的阳台朝南，阳光很充足。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de yángtái cháo nán, yángguāng hěn chōngzú.
examples.english: My home's balcony faces south and gets plenty of sunlight.

examples.hanzi: 他们在阳台上喝茶聊天。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài yángtái shàng hē chá liáotiān.
examples.english: They drink tea and chat on the balcony.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 这只是我的一点心意,请收下。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǐshì wǒ de yìdiǎn xīnyì, qǐng shōuxià.
example.english: This is just a small token of my regard — please accept it.
example.fact: In many East Asian cultures, gifts for weddings and New Year celebrations are traditionally wrapped in red paper, since red is associated with luck and prosperity, while white wrapping is generally avoided because of its association with mourning.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你的心意，我很感动。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de xīnyì, wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: Thank you for your kindness; I'm very touched.

examples.hanzi: 这份礼物虽然小，但是表达了我的心意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn lǐwù suīrán xiǎo, dànshì biǎodá le wǒ de xīnyì.
examples.english: Although this gift is small, it expresses my feelings.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
禾 (grain) — marks grain and crops, as in 秋, 种, 租; 称 originally meant weighing grain, then naming (称呼).

example.hanzi: 他自称是这家公司的创始人。
example.pinyin: tā zìchēng shì zhè jiā gōngsī de chuàngshǐrén.
example.english: He claims to be the founder of this company.
example.fact: Anna Anderson was one of several women who, over several decades, claimed to be Grand Duchess Anastasia, the youngest daughter of Russia's last tsar, believed killed with her family in 1918. DNA testing conducted in the 1990s proved that Anderson was unrelated to the Romanov family.

examples.hanzi: 那个人自称是医生，可是没人相信。
examples.pinyin: Nàge rén zìchēng shì yīshēng, kěshì méi rén xiāngxìn.
examples.english: That man claims to be a doctor, but nobody believes him.

examples.hanzi: 她自称不喜欢甜食，却天天吃蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā zìchēng bù xǐhuan tiánshí, què tiāntiān chī dàngāo.
examples.english: She claims not to like sweets, yet eats cake every day.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 哈 is the sound of laughing.
合 (hé) — near sound — 哈 is hā; 合 also sounds out 盒 hé.
罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 哈罗德是我在伦敦认识的朋友。
example.pinyin: Hāluódé shì wǒ zài Lúndūn rènshi de péngyou.
example.english: Harold is a friend I met in London.
example.fact: Harrods, the London department store whose name derives from founder Charles Henry Harrod, opened as a small grocery shop in 1834 and grew into one of the world's largest department stores, spanning more than a million square feet across five floors.

examples.hanzi: 哈罗德今天请我们吃晚饭。
examples.pinyin: Hāluódé jīntiān qǐng wǒmen chī wǎnfàn.
examples.english: Harold is treating us to dinner today.

examples.hanzi: 我想把这本书送给哈罗德。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ zhè běn shū sòng gěi Hāluódé.
examples.english: I want to give this book to Harold.

components.note: 田 (field) — 画 (simplified 畫) originally showed a brush 聿 drawing the borders of a field: to draw lines, hence a picture.
田 (field) — 画 (simplified 畫) originally showed a brush 聿 drawing the borders of a field: to draw lines, hence a picture.

example.hanzi: 我妹妹喜欢画画。
example.pinyin: wǒ mèimei xǐhuan huàhuà.
example.english: My younger sister likes to draw.
example.fact: The Cave of Altamira in Spain contains paintings of bison and other animals created more than 14,000 years ago using natural pigments such as ochre and charcoal. Discovered in 1868, it is sometimes called the 'Sistine Chapel of Paleolithic art.'

examples.hanzi: 他在公园里给孩子们画画。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngyuán lǐ gěi háizimen huà huà.
examples.english: He is drawing pictures for the kids in the park.

examples.hanzi: 她从五岁起就开始画画了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng wǔ suì qǐ jiù kāishǐ huàhuà le.
examples.english: She has been drawing since she was five.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.

example.hanzi: 那座火山已经沉睡了两百年。
example.pinyin: nà zuò huǒshān yǐjīng chénshuìle liǎng bǎi nián.
example.english: That volcano has been dormant for two hundred years.
example.fact: Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption in Indonesia was the most powerful in recorded history, ejecting so much ash and sulfur into the atmosphere that it cooled global temperatures and made 1816 known as the 'Year Without a Summer' across Europe and North America.

examples.hanzi: 火山突然喷发了，浓烟冲上天空。
examples.pinyin: Huǒshān tūrán pēnfā le, nóngyān chōng shàng tiānkōng.
examples.english: The volcano suddenly erupted, and thick smoke shot into the sky.

examples.hanzi: 我们爬上了一座活火山。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen pá shàng le yí zuò huó huǒshān.
examples.english: We climbed a volcano that is still active.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 他把这个问题反映给了上级。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zhège wèntí fǎnyìng gěile shàngjí.
example.english: He reported the problem to his superiors.
example.fact: Stanley Milgram's 1961 obedience experiments at Yale found that a majority of participants were willing to administer what they believed were painful electric shocks to a stranger simply because an authority figure in a lab coat instructed them to keep going.

examples.hanzi: 我的上级今天要来检查工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shàngjí jīntiān yào lái jiǎnchá gōngzuò.
examples.english: My superior is coming to check on the work today.

examples.hanzi: 下级要听从上级的安排。
examples.pinyin: Xiàjí yào tīngcóng shàngjí de ānpái.
examples.english: Subordinates should follow their superiors' arrangements.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — a picture of an ox's head with horns; as a radical it marks cattle, in 牺, 牲, 牧, 物.
亻 (person) — person radical, used for 仔 as "small creature or child", as in 牛仔 cowboy and 仔细 careful.
子 (zǐ) — same sound — 仔 is zǐ; 子 also means child, so sound and meaning agree.
衤 (clothing, 衣字旁) — clothes: 衬 shirt, 衫, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt; 裤 is trousers.
库 (kù) sounds exactly like 裤.

example.hanzi: 他穿着一条蓝色的牛仔裤。
example.pinyin: tā chuānzhe yī tiáo lán sè de niúzǎikù.
example.english: He is wearing a pair of blue jeans.
example.fact: Levi Strauss and tailor Jacob Davis patented the use of copper rivets to reinforce denim work pants in 1873, creating the modern blue jean. The rivets were placed at stress points like pocket corners to keep the pants from tearing during hard labor.

examples.hanzi: 这条牛仔裤我穿着有点紧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo niúzǎikù wǒ chuānzhe yǒudiǎn jǐn.
examples.english: These jeans are a bit tight on me.

examples.hanzi: 牛仔裤配白衬衫很好看。
examples.pinyin: Niúzǎikù pèi bái chènshān hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: Jeans with a white shirt look nice.

components.note: 氵 (water) — a stream to cross; also in 河 river, 游 swim.
步 (step) — steps through water: wading, hence being involved in something.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women and feelings in old forms, as in 妒, 嫉; 嫌 is to dislike.
兼 (jiān) — near sound — 嫌 is xián; 兼 also sounds out 谦 qiān and 歉 qiàn.

example.hanzi: 他涉嫌参与了这起诈骗案。
example.pinyin: tā shèxián cānyùle zhè qǐ zhàpiàn àn.
example.english: He is suspected of being involved in this fraud case.
example.fact: The term 'Ponzi scheme' comes from Charles Ponzi, who defrauded investors in Boston in 1920 by promising 50 percent returns within 45 days. He paid earlier investors with money collected from new ones until the scheme collapsed within about a year.

examples.hanzi: 他涉嫌酒后驾车，被警察带走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shèxián jiǔ hòu jiàchē, bèi jǐngchá dàizǒu le.
examples.english: He is suspected of drunk driving and was taken away by the police.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司涉嫌偷税。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī shèxián tōushuì.
examples.english: This company is suspected of tax evasion.
